# gamarr

**gamarr** finds great games and puts them in your library — no browsing,
no manual searches, no cleanup. A configurable pipeline scrapes Metacritic
for critically-acclaimed releases, filters out unwanted genres and keywords,
matches titles against FitGirl repacks and FreeGOG, and delivers
torrents to qBittorrent. Once downloads complete, a post-processing thread
SHA-256-verifies and copies each game to your library with customizable path
templates, then cleans up source torrents. Runs as a daemon so your library
stays fresh without lifting a finger.

## Features

- **Two-phase score verification** — browse pages use internal Metacritic
  metrics (not real 0–100 scores) to build a candidate pool quickly.
  Browse scores are on a completely different scale (e.g. 1478, 1931) and
  **always pass** the configured thresholds — the real 0–100 score
  filtering only happens during the detail-page verification step.
  This avoids hundreds of slow HTTP requests while keeping score accuracy.
- **Genre-based rejection** — exclude games by genre using case-insensitive
  substring matching (e.g. `["RPG"]` rejects "Action RPG", "JRPG", etc.).
- **Keyword-based filtering** — reject games whose titles or FitGirl page
  description contain specific keywords.
- **Date-based backlog cutoff** — set the oldest month to review with
  `max_date: 202401` and how much of the backlog one cycle covers with
  `max_cycle_months: 2`. Pages remain available as `max_pages` /
  `max_cycle_pages` for `criticscore`/`userscore`, whose browse lists are
  score-ordered and have no date dimension.
- **Verify before queueing** — a game's real Metacritic detail-page scores are
  checked *before* it enters the pending queue, so the queue only ever holds
  games that already pass the thresholds. Games that fail, or whose scores are
  not published yet, are not queued: they are re-checked when a browse pass next
  reaches their pages (immediately in `latest` mode, when the sweep wraps in
  `backlog` mode) instead of occupying the queue for days.
- **Source-matching expiry** — a queued (already verified) game waits
  `download_sites.fitgirl.max_queue_days` for a matching repack (default 60, or
  `0` for indefinite; the FitGirl entry supplies the window for every queued
  game). Every game is queued already verified, so it takes that window at
  insert, and later re-checks do not push the window forward, so a verified game
  with no match still leaves the queue when the window lapses. Without a FitGirl

# Design: explicit discovery modes, verify-before-queue, and an honest keyword scope

Date: 2026-11-06
Status: Approved (user agreed each decision in session)

## Goal

Make discovery predictable and stop the queue accumulating games that can never pass.

Three symptoms were reported and then measured against the live instance (867 cycles of
`gamarr.log`, the live `gamarr.db`, and live fetches of FitGirl pages):

1. No new games are delivered, and older games appear only sporadically.
2. The user cannot tell what the daemon is doing, because "mode" is an emergent
   consequence of `max_date` / `max_pages` / `max_cycle_*` rather than a stated choice.
3. The pending queue holds 1,555 rows, 1,534 of which can never pass verification
   (16,896 rows have expired all-time against 63 deliveries).

The intended behaviour is two explicit modes: a **latest** mode that looks at the newest
releases, and a **backlog** mode that sweeps back through older ones, with critic/user
score sorting applying to both.

## What was measured (and what corrected the original diagnosis)

- **The `hv` keyword accounts for most match rejections**: 7,821 skips on `hv`, 1,817 on
  `emulator`, 771 on `hypervisor` in the current log. All 21 games that passed Metacritic
  verification were blocked — Wukong, Metaphor, RE Requiem, Forza Horizon 6, Crimson Desert,
  Jurassic World Evolution 3 and others.
- **Most of those rejections are correct.** FitGirl's "Repack Features" block for Black Myth:
  Wukong reads *"Hypervisor Bypass (INTEL & AMD) by DenuvOwO + Goldberg emu added … Custom
  launcher added for easier HV steps processing"*. Metaphor and Crimson Desert carry the
  same bypass line. These are genuinely HV repacks.
- **A minority are false positives.** Resident Evil Requiem and Forza Horizon 6 have no
  `hv`/`hypervisor`/`emulator` in their Repack Features block; they are rejected on
  download-mirror boilerplate at the top of the page (*"Only updated files for a new non-HV
  repack"*, *"convert your INSTALLED HV version"*).
- **The scope is also upside down.** On the Wukong page the boilerplate sits at characters
  476 and 1027, `Backwards Compatibility` (today's truncation point) at 2221, and
  `Repack Features` at 4914. The current code discards the authoritative section and keeps
  the text that causes false positives.

# Discovery Modes, Verify-Before-Queue, and Keyword Scope — Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use sub-agents (recommended) to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Make gamarr's discovery predictable — an explicit `mode: latest | backlog`, queue only games that already pass detail verification, and match reject keywords against the FitGirl "Repack Features" block with whole-word/negation rules instead of a substring scan of the whole article.

**Architecture:** Four coupled changes, sequenced so the delivery blocker lands first: (1) keyword scope extractor, (2) whole-word/negation matcher wired into `_check_reject_keywords`, (3) one-time queue migration plus `record_pending(score_checks_passed=...)`, (4) verify-before-insert inside `_process_browse_games`, (5) `mode` config + pipeline plumbing, (6) the latest-mode branch in the existing year loop, (7) README. Discovery stays Metacritic-first; no new network surface beyond one detail lookup per new candidate.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3.12, pydantic v2, SQLAlchemy + SQLite, loguru, pytest, ruff, mypy, `uv`.

**Spec:** `docs/agent/specs/2026-11-06-discovery-modes-and-queue-hygiene-design.md` (approved).

**Commit policy:** when this plan runs inside the chain, do **not** commit between tasks — the finalising step owns commits. The commit steps below are for standalone execution.

1. **The "heading-like line" terminator cannot be implemented.** `_fetch_fitgirl_page_content` collapses whitespace in the extracted article, so there are no newlines to anchor a colon-terminated heading. ## Context synthesis — gamarr

- **What it is:** `/data/gamarr`, branch `main`, at `4d8b745` (v3.4.1). A Python 3.12/uv daemon that scrapes Metacritic for acclaimed releases, filters genre/keyword rejects, matches titles against FitGirl/FreeGOG, delivers to qBittorrent, then SHA-256-verifies and copies to a templated library path. Config is YAML with in-place migration.
- **Working tree state:** four uncommitted files — `src/gamarr/pipeline.py`, `tests/unit/test_pipeline.py`, `README.md`, `docs/agent/specs/2026-11-06-discovery-modes-and-queue-hygiene-design.md`. That is the change under review (latest-mode date driving).

## Review

**Scope:** full `/tmp/review-diff.txt` (441 lines) plus the surrounding code in `src/gamarr/pipeline.py`, `src/gamarr/metacritic.py`, `tests/unit/test_pipeline.py`, `README.md`, `docs/agent/specs/2026-11-06-discovery-modes-and-queue-hygiene-design.md`, `src/gamarr/config.py`, `src/gamarr/scheduler.py`. No files modified.

### Correct (verified, with evidence)

- **Latest never reads or writes cursors in the new date path.** `start_page = 1 if latest_mode` (`pipeline.py:660`), page writes guarded by `if pages_scanned > 0 and not latest_mode` (`pipeline.py:726`), and both `reset_progress` calls are inside `if date_mode and not latest_mode` / `elif not latest_mode` (`pipeline.py:794-820`). The budget-auto-reset `db.reset_progress` (`:630`) is only reachable in the non-latest/non-date branch. So a date-driven latest cycle cannot corrupt or reset backlog cursors, and `test_backlog_after_latest_resets_cursors_from_another_order` still guards the flip-back case.
- **`_date_driven` cannot disagree with the pipeline.** `run_acquisition` computes it from the *normalised* `mode` and `"new" if mode == "latest" else sort_order` (`pipeline.py:368-374`); `_run_discovery_phases` computes `date_mode` from `scan_order` (already coerced to `"new"` for latest) and `cfg.sort_order` (`pipeline.py:487`). Both inputs are identical, so `_normalise_latest_depth`'s `date_driven` and the scan's `date_mode` always agree.
- **Backlog semantics are unchanged.** `_date_driven("new", False, max_date, ·)` reduces to the old `bool(cfg.max_date) and scan_order == "new"`; the `date_mode` call-shape block now runs before the latest branch but previously ran as `elif date_mode` for backlog with identical body (`cutoff_date = floor_cutoff`, `month_span_left = 0`, `per_call_max = 0`; `pipeline.py:662-680`); `if floor_month:` (`:716`) is equivalent to the old `if date_mode:` because `floor_month = cfg.max_date if date_mode else 0` (`:486`); score sorts still land in the `year=0`/`cutoff_date=None` page path (`:602-608`, `:692-701`).
- **Primitive reuse is sound.** `cutoff_date = max(pace_cutoff, floor_cutoff) if floor_cutoff else pace_cutoff` (`pipeline.py:676-677`) is correct, and `_effective_cutoff` compares *parsed* dates (`metacritic.py:1099-1113`), so the ISO-vs-DD-MM ambiguity can't bite. `floor_stop` vs `_recent_games_stop_cutoff` (`:763`) correctly distinguishes a pace stop from floor completion.
- **`max_pages=0` reaching the client is safe.** `_page_limit_reached` only fires for `max_pages > 0` (`metacritic.py:1173`) and the fetch loop is hard-bounded by `page_number <= 2000` (`metacritic.py:944`); 0 already means "no page cap" in the pre-existing page-mode path. No crash, no infinite loop.
- **The new tests are not vacuous.** They inspect the client kwargs captured by the fake (`calls[0]["max_pages"]`, `max_month_span`, `cutoff_date`, and `{call["year"]}`), so each would fail against the pre-diff code (e.g. `calls[0]["max_pages"]` would have been `2`, not `0`). `TestDateDrivenResolution` pins the predicate matrix directly.
- **Docs match the code.** README rows 191-195 and the diff's spec table cell-for-cell describe what the implementation does, including "`0` = read it all" for `max_date` without a pace.

### Findings

**1. MEDIUM — the year-range lower bound is derived from *today's* month, so the pace window can be silently truncated.**
`src/gamarr/pipeline.py:590-593`.
```python
pace_year = subtract_months(current_year_month(), cfg.max_cycle_months) // 100
cutoff_year = max(pace_year, floor_year) if floor_year else pace_year
```
The comment claims today is "the widest possible anchor", but the client anchors the pace on the newest month of the **actual** first dated page (`_next_span_anchor` → `_page_newest_month`, `metacritic.py:1055-1084`), and browse listings are strictly year-scoped (`releaseYearMin=releaseYearMax=<year>`, `metacritic.py:834-843`). If the current year's listing is empty or stale (every January before the first release; months-long quiet spell; a niche platform), the anchor `A` is older than today's month, so the real cutoff `A - pace` falls into a year *below* the loop's bound and is never probed.
Concrete: `mode: latest`, `max_cycle_months: 12`, cycle on 2026-01-05, no 2026 releases yet, newest 2025 game dated 2025-12-19. `pace_year = 2025`, loop = {2026, 2025}. The 2025 call anchors at 2025-12 and computes cutoff 2024-12, so the configured window reaches into 2024-12 — but 2024 is never scanned. Those Dec-2024 releases are dropped every January cycle and cannot be recovered later (once a 2026 release appears the anchor moves forward and they legitimately fall out). Same shape with `max_cycle_months: 1200` on a dead platform, where the loop can be several years too shallow.
Fix: pad the bound (`cutoff_year = max(pace_year - 1, floor_year)` — costs at most one extra first-page probe, which trips the cutoff immediately), or derive the bound from a conservative (oldest plausible) anchor. File: `src/gamarr/pipeline.py`.
Note on severity: the README frames `max_cycle_months` as "how far back one cycle reads" (a cap), and latest's core promise (new releases always seen) still holds, so I did not raise this to HIGH; the defect is that the *shortening is driven by an unrelated quantity* (today's month vs. the listing's newest month) and is silent.

**2. MEDIUM — a new test hard-codes the current year and will fail from 2027-01-01.**
`tests/unit/test_pipeline.py:9890-9895`:
```python
calls, logs = self._run(tmp_path=tmp_path, max_pages=3, max_date=202601, max_cycle_months=24)
assert {call["year"] for call in calls} == {2026}, calls
```
Nothing freezes the clock (no `freeze_time` in the file or `tests/conftest.py`). On 2027-01-01 `max_date=202601` is still valid and not in the future, `floor_year = 2026`, `pace_year = 2024`, so `cutoff_year = 2026`, `current_year = 2027` and the loop legitimately probes 2027 **and** 2026 → the exact-equality assertion fails. The test's stated intent ("must not probe 2024/2025") is over-specified into "must probe only 2026". Every other year-sensitive test in the file derives the year from `datetime.datetime.now(tz=datetime.UTC).year` (e.g. `:9830`, `:9930`).
Fix: assert the absence instead: `assert min(call["year"] for call in calls) >= 2026` (plus `not any(y in {2024, 2025} ...)`). Also note the second assertion in that test (`not any("mis-indexed" ...)`) is vacuous — the fake never sets `_recent_games_cutoff_reached`. File: `tests/unit/test_pipeline.py`.

**3. MEDIUM — a date-driven latest cycle has no per-cycle page ceiling and re-reads it *every* cycle.**
`src/gamarr/pipeline.py:667` (`per_call_max = 0`) combined with `:565-571` (the `max_pages` "unused" path) and `:649` (the depth break is skipped when `date_mode`).
The only ceilings left are the client's per-call `2000`-page guard (`metacritic.py:944`) and the number of years in `cutoff_year..current_year`. Ask: what does one cycle cost?
- `mode: latest`, `max_date: 195801` (documented minimum), no pace → **every cycle** walks 69 year listings with no page cap and no cursor (backlog at least advances and then resets). `browse_games` accumulates every game in the window before `_process_browse_games`, so tens of thousands of dicts are resident (`pipeline.py:713-718`, `:829-844`).
- `mode: latest`, `max_cycle_months: 1200` (accepted at config load, `config.py:127`) → ~101 year listings per cycle, every cycle.
- Migration angle: `max_date` in latest mode was previously documented as "informational; depth decides", and `max_pages` still capped the cycle. An existing `mode: latest` + `max_date` config silently switches from ≤`max_pages` pages/cycle to the whole window per cycle; the operator's only lever (`max_pages`) is now explicitly bypassed.
Not a crash and not unbounded in the strict sense, but it is a real, repeating cost on a critical path (discovery runs on the scheduler) with no safety valve.
Fix: pass an absolute per-cycle page ceiling in latest date mode (a constant, or keep `max_pages` as a hard ceiling while `max_date`/pace decide depth) and/or cap the year span. File: `src/gamarr/pipeline.py`.

**4. MEDIUM — the two invariants this change is about are untested for the date-driven path.**
`tests/unit/test_pipeline.py:9859-9907`. The new latest tests assert call shape and logs, but:
- `test_does_not_persist_cursors` (`:9825`) only exercises **depth** mode; no new test runs a date-driven latest cycle and asserts `db.get_last_scanned_page(...) == 0` / a seeded mid-sweep cursor is untouched. That is the explicit intent statement ("must still never read or write cursors") and the guard at `pipeline.py:726` is one `and not` away from regressing.
- `test_a_floor_alone_bounds_latest_without_pacing` (`:9882`) never asserts `call["year"]`, so a regression that only probed the current year (dropping the floor entirely) would still pass. The paced case is pinned (`:9894`); the unpaced floor case is not.
Fix: add `assert all(c["year"] >= 2024 for c in calls)` there, and one date-driven cursor test. File: `tests/unit/test_pipeline.py`.

**5. LOW — the negative-`max_pages` clamp is now skipped in *backlog* date mode too.**
`src/gamarr/pipeline.py:373` passes `date_driven=True` for backlog (`_date_driven("new", False, 202401, ·)` is `True`), so `_normalise_latest_depth` (`:240-241`) returns `-5` untouched where it previously warned and substituted 500. Harmless today (`cfg.max_pages` is inert in backlog date mode, `:553`, `:610`), but it silently drops a diagnostic that exists specifically for direct API callers. Fix: gate on `mode == "latest"` in the early return, or compute the flag as `mode == "latest" and _date_driven(...)`. File: `src/gamarr/pipeline.py`.

**6. LOW — dead branch in the new year-range logic.**
`src/gamarr/pipeline.py:594-595`: `else: cutoff_year = floor_year or scan_year_anchor - 1`. This `else` runs only when `cfg.max_cycle_months == 0`, and `date_mode` for latest then requires `max_date`, so `floor_year` is always non-zero. The `scan_year_anchor - 1` fallback is unreachable and reads as if an unpaced floorless latest cycle could get here. Fix: `cutoff_year = floor_year` plus a short comment. def test_a_pace_wider_than_the_floor_does_not_walk_below_it(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        """A pace that reaches past the floor must not open years below it."""
        from gamarr.utils import current_year_month

        floor_month = (current_year_month() // 100) * 100 + 1  # January of this year
        calls, _logs = self._run(tmp_path=tmp_path, max_pages=3, max_date=floor_month, max_cycle_months=24)
        assert calls
        years = {call["year"] for call in calls}
        assert floor_month // 100 in years, f"the floor year must still be probed: {years}"
        assert min(years) >= floor_month // 100, f"the pace must not open years below the floor: {years}"

    def test_the_pace_bound_keeps_one_year_of_anchor_slack(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        """The client anchors on the newest release it sees, which can lag today."""

- **Floorless paced descent to 1958 — cost and stop.** Bounded and correct, not unbounded. An empty year costs exactly **one** page‑1 GET: page 1 with an empty parse never re-probes (`_needs_drain_confirmation` requires `page_number > 1`, `metacritic.py:1040‑1054`), `_classify_page` returns `None` (`:618‑639`) and `_finish_scan` reports 0 pages (`:985‑1027`). The descent stops on the first *dated* page older than the pace cut: `_page_stop_decision` sets `_recent_games_cutoff_reached` + `_recent_games_stop_cutoff` (`metacritic.py:1115‑1157`), the pipeline breaks (`pipeline.py:816‑817`), and `floor_cutoff is None` in floorless mode means `floor_stop` can never mask the break (`:794`).     bound must not depend on today's month alone (see the year-range branch), and
    it must never go below the catalogue's first year: a listing that carries no
    release dates at all would otherwise be crawled for decades every cycle.

    Args:
        max_cycle_months: The configured month pace; always positive here.
        current_year: The cycle's current year.

    Returns:
        The oldest year to probe.
    """
    pace_years = math.ceil(max_cycle_months / 12)
    return max(EARLIEST_BROWSE_YEAR, current_year - (pace_years + _FLOORLESS_LATEST_SLACK_YEARS))

def test_the_year_bound_is_the_floor_not_a_derived_bound(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        """A stale anchor must not be truncated by a bound derived from today."""
        # A floor far below the pace window: only the floor may set the bound.
        def games(year: int) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
            # Listings are empty until the floor year, so the pace anchor lags today.
            if year <= 2020:
                return [{"title": "G", "slug": "g", "release_date": f"{year}-12-01"}]
            return []

        calls, _logs = self._run(
            tmp_path=tmp_path,
            max_pages=3,
            max_date=202001,
            max_cycle_months=12,
            games_for_year=games,
        )
        years = [call["year"] for call in calls]
        assert 2020 in years, f"the loop must descend to the floor year to reach a stale anchor: {years}"
        assert min(years) == 2020, f"the floor year is the bottom of the window: {years}"

    def test_a_floorless_pace_reaches_below_empty_recent_listings(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        """Recent years with no dated game must not truncate the pace window."""
        import datetime

        current_year = datetime.datetime.now(tz=datetime.UTC).year
        first_dated_year = current_year - 3

        def games(year: int) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
            if year <= first_dated_year:
                return [{"title": "G", "slug": "g", "release_date": f"{year}-12-01"}]
            return []

        calls, _logs = self._run(
            tmp_path=tmp_path,
            max_pages=3,
            max_cycle_months=12,
            games_for_year=games,
        )
        years = [call["year"] for call in calls]
        assert first_dated_year in years, f"the loop must descend past the empty listings to the anchor: {years}"
        assert min(years) >= 1958, f"a floorless cycle must never probe below the catalogue's first year: {years}"

    def test_a_floorless_pace_stops_at_the_catalogue_floor(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        """With no dates anywhere the descent must not run for decades."""
        calls, _logs = self._run(
            tmp_path=tmp_path,
            max_pages=3,
            max_cycle_months=1,
            games_for_year=lambda _year: [],
        )
        years = [call["year"] for call in calls]
        assert years, "expected at least one probe"
        assert min(years) >= 1958, years
        assert len(years) <= 6, f"a floorless deadline must bound the descent, got {len(years)} probes: {years}"

    def test_a_coerced_score_sort_still_uses_the_date_window(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        """latest coerces the sort to 'new' first, so its date keys must apply."""
        calls, logs = self._run(
            tmp_path=tmp_path, max_pages=3, max_date=202401, max_cycle_months=2, sort_order="criticscore"
        )
        assert calls
        assert calls[0]["max_pages"] == 0, "the page cap must be dropped even after a coerced sort"
        assert calls[0]["max_month_span"] == 2
        assert calls[0]["cutoff_date"] == "2024-01-01"
        assert any("latest mode requires sort_order 'new'" in line.lower() for line in logs), logs

I could not execute anything (no shell), so the commands to run are listed at the end.

**No HIGH-severity finding.** The three MEDIUM items are listed first.

### Correct (verified, not assumed)

- **Round-3 fix 1 (year bound).** `pipeline.py:619-633`: floored latest is bounded by `floor_month // 100`, floorless latest by `_floorless_latest_bound(cfg.max_cycle_months, scan_year_anchor)`; neither is today's *month*-derived. The slack arithmetic is self-consistent: `bound ≤ anchor_year − pace_years` for any anchor within `_FLOORLESS_LATEST_SLACK_YEARS`, and `max(EARLIEST_BROWSE_YEAR, …)` (`pipeline.py:201-220`) stops a no-date listing from being crawled for decades.
- **Round-3 fix 2 (outage guard).** `pipeline.py:693-702` sits inside `elif date_mode:` and only for `latest_mode`; `_recent_games_failed` is reset at the top of every `scan_recent_games` call (`metacritic.py:938-941`), so a *stale* failure flag cannot trip it. It cannot fire on the first iteration, and `is_cancelled` breaks first.
- **Round-3 fix 3 (undated warning).** `pipeline.py:841-848` requires `pages_this_cycle > 0`, which excludes the healthy "empty listing" case (an empty page 1 gives `last_page = 0` → `pages_scanned = 0`, `metacritic.py:985-1020`), so it cannot fire on a quiet site.
- **Round-3 fix 4 (constant).** `utils.py:200-206,231`: `is_valid_year_month` keeps byte-identical semantics (`195801 ≤ v ≤ 999912`, `1 ≤ v%100 ≤ 12`, `bool` rejected), so the validator and the config migrators behave exactly as before.
- **Round-3 fix 5 (tests).** Stale-anchor, floorless-cap, outage and coerced-sort tests each fail if their fix is reverted — except the coerced-sort one (LOW 2 below).
- **No latest-mode cursor writes.** `set_last_scanned_page` is guarded at `pipeline.py:773`, and all three `reset_progress` sites (`559`, `668`, `866/876`) are behind `not latest_mode`; `latest` only writes `last_sort_order` (`database.py:719-727`), which does not touch `BacklogProgress`. The date-driven path reuses `start_page = 1` and `per_call_max = 0`, so it inherits that invariant.
- **Backlog semantics unchanged.** `_date_driven` returns `bool(max_date)` for backlog (`pipeline.py:222-244`), so `date_mode` is the old predicate; the reordered call-shape branch produces identical `cutoff_date`/`max_month_span`/`per_call_max`, the `max()` in `pipeline.py:723-724` is None-safeguarded only for the new floorless-latest case, and the `if date_mode:` → `if floor_month:` filter change is a no-op in backlog (floor ≠ 0 iff date mode). Pre-existing backlog tests (`TestDateModeResolution`, including `test_max_cycle_months_without_max_date_is_inert`) still hold because they run `mode="backlog"`.
- **Docs match code** for the config table rows (`README.md:191-195`), the phase-1 prose, the spec table/window branch, and the plan's superseded note.

### Findings

**MEDIUM 1 — An unpaced date-driven latest cycle has no page cap of any kind; a legacy config silently loses its `max_pages` bound.**
`src/gamarr/pipeline.py:709-731` sets `per_call_max = 0` for *every* date-mode call, and the year loop's only page check is the depth-mode one at `pipeline.py:687-689`; the descent bound is the floor year (`619-633`), so every calendar year from today down to the floor is crawled to its end.
Failure scenario (config that was valid and bounded before this diff): `mode: latest`, `max_date: 202001`, `max_pages: 50`. Before: `≤ 50` pages/cycle (`_latest_call_depth`, old branch). After: the entire 2020→2026 window each cycle — that is a several-fold increase in fetches plus a detail-verification pass per game. With the documented maximum `max_date: 195801`, the cycle cannot finish inside `acquisition_timeout_mins` (`scheduler.py:64-108`), so every cycle is aborted by the watchdog while the detached pipeline thread keeps fetching, and the next cycle starts another full descent from the top. The behaviour is documented and warned about (`pipeline.py:604-615`), so it may be intended — but the *regression* for an existing `max_pages`-capped config is not, and the warning does not say the cap was ignored. Smallest fix (one branch): in the date branch, when `latest_mode and not cfg.max_cycle_months`, keep `per_call_max = max_pages_cfg` as a safety cap instead of `0`; or, if the design must keep `max_pages` inert, state the migration risk in the `max_pages` README row. File: `src/gamarr/pipeline.py` (+`README.md`).

**MEDIUM 2 — The floorless bound can truncate the documented pace window with no diagnostic at all.**
`_floorless_latest_bound` (`pipeline.py:201-220`, used at `629-632`) stops the descent at `current_year − (ceil(pace/12) + 3)`.
Failure scenario: `mode: latest`, `max_cycle_months: 6`, platform whose newest listing year is `current_year − 5` (any quiet/legacy platform: the listing years above the newest release return an empty parse). Every probed year yields `pages_scanned == 0`, so `pages_this_cycle == 0` and the round-3 undated warning at `pipeline.py:841-848` is skipped by its own `pages_this_cycle > 0` condition; there is no other log. The cycle collects nothing, silently, forever, although `README.md:195` promises "how far back one cycle reads, counted in months from the cycle's newest release month". Smallest fix: after the loop, warn when `latest_mode and date_mode and not floor_month and max_month_seen is None` (or when the descent stopped at the synthetic bound without any dated page) and name the bound year. File: `src/gamarr/pipeline.py`.

**MEDIUM 3 — The undated-cycle warning (round-3 fix 3) has no test.**
`src/gamarr/pipeline.py:841-848`. Fix 5 lists tests for four of the five fixes; this one is unexercised, so a future edit to the condition (e.g. dropping `pages_this_cycle > 0`, or moving it out of `cfg.enabled`) would pass the suite. The helper already supports it: `games_for_year=lambda _y: [{"title": "G", "slug": "g"}]` (undated) makes `pages_this_cycle > 0` and `max_month_seen is None`; assert the warning text and, separately, that an empty-listing cycle (`games_for_year=lambda _y: []`) does *not* warn. File: `tests/unit/test_pipeline.py` (`TestLatestMode`).

**LOW 1 — `test_a_pace_wider_than_the_floor_does_not_walk_below_it` is vacuous.**
`tests/unit/test_pipeline.py:9905-9912` sets `floor_month` to January of the *current* year, so `cutoff_year == scan_year_anchor` and the loop has exactly one iteration. Both assertions (`floor year in years`, `min(years) >= floor year`) hold regardless of what the bound does. The rule is genuinely pinned by `test_the_year_bound_is_the_floor_not_a_derived_bound` (`9920-9940`), so this is duplicate-only coverage; making it meaningful needs `max_date=202001, max_cycle_months=2` so the window spans several years. File: `tests/unit/test_pipeline.py`.

**LOW 2 — The coerced-sort test does not pin the coercion it names.**
`tests/unit/test_pipeline.py:9975-9985` uses `max_pages=3`, but in date mode the call's `max_pages` is `0` regardless (`pipeline.py:715`), so all four assertions still pass if `run_acquisition` computes `_date_driven` from the raw `sort_order` (`pipeline.py:400`) instead of `"new" if mode == "latest"`. The only observable difference of that bug is a spurious `clamping depth to 10` warning plus `cfg.max_pages=10`. Smallest fix: pass `max_pages=0` and assert `not any("clamping" in line.lower() for line in logs)`. File: `tests/unit/test_pipeline.py`.

**LOW 3 — The 1958 floor is only partly a single constant.**
`src/gamarr/utils.py:200` now defines `EARLIEST_BROWSE_YEAR`, but the literal survives at `src/gamarr/config.py:139` (docstring) and `:154` (the `ValueError` message users see) and at `src/gamarr/metacritic.py:838` (all-time `releaseYearMin`). Changing the constant would leave the validator's message self-contradictory. Files: `src/gamarr/config.py`, `src/gamarr/metacritic.py`.

**LOW 4 — The "unpaced" warning misses effectively-unpaced paces.**
`src/gamarr/pipeline.py:604-615` only warns when `max_cycle_months == 0`. `max_cycle_months: 1200` (the documented maximum, accepted by `config.py:127`) is equally uncapped in practice — `_floorless_latest_bound` becomes 1958 and the pace cutoff is a century back — yet no warning is emitted. File: `src/gamarr/pipeline.py`.

**LOW 5 — README phase-1 text is inaccurate for a `max_date`-only latest cycle.**
`README.md:323-325`: "it reads back at most `max_cycle_months` months from the newest release". With `max_date` set and `max_cycle_months: 0` the cycle reads the *whole* window (0 means unpaced), so "at most 0 months" is the opposite of what happens. File: `README.md`.

**LOW 6 — The undated warning can misdiagnose, and can fire on a cancelled cycle.**
`pipeline.py:763-764` drops below-floor games *before* the month tracking at `790-800`, so a cycle whose collected pages carried dates that were all below `floor_month` (kept only because of undated entries on the same page) logs "Browse pages carried no release dates", which is false. It can also fire when the loop broke on `is_cancelled` at `685`. File: `src/gamarr/pipeline.py`.

**LOW 7 — The spec's pseudocode computes `date_driven` before the latest→`"new"` coercion.**
`docs/agent/specs/2026-11-06-discovery-modes-and-queue-hygiene-design.md` ("Mode resolution", `date_driven = _date_driven(scan_order, …)` placed above `scan_order = "new" if cfg.mode == "latest" …`) contradicts the implementation (`pipeline.py:400` deliberately passes `"new"` for latest) and invites the exact bug LOW 2 fails to catch. File: the spec doc.

### Tests the supervisor must run

- `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_pipeline.py -q -k "LatestMode or DateDrivenResolution or NegativePageBudget or DateModeResolution"` (confirms both the new date-driven latest cases and the untouched backlog date-mode suite).
- `uv run pytest tests/unit -q` (full unit suite, incl. `test_readme_accuracy.py`, `test_config.py`, `test_metacritic.py`).
- `uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check . && uv run mypy src` (pre-commit parity; `pipeline.py:400` is 119 chars, so no E501/format issue that I could find).

Smallest fix (one file, `src/gamarr/pipeline.py`): require evidence of a *run-wide* outage before abandoning the cycle — e.g. break only after 2 consecutive failed years, or only when the failure repeats on the next year down. Independent year listings make "year N failed" a poor proxy for "blind descent".

`pipeline.py:717-760` (`per_call_max = 0`), `pipeline.py:852-861` (warning only *after* the loop), `metacritic.py:944` (only bound left is 2000 pages/call).

A date bound is the *only* per-call stop for a date-driven latest cycle (`_page_is_before_cutoff` requires `dates_found`, `metacritic.py:484-499`). If Metacritic keeps returning games but drops `release_date` (the markup-change shape the comment at `:853-856` names), no cutoff and no span can ever fire, so each call pages to the end of that year's listing (~16–866 pages per the design note), and the year loop descends over the whole window (`current_year - floor_year + 1` years — e.g. 12 years for `max_date: 201501`). That is thousands of fetches every cycle, where the pre-diff latest config was capped at `max_pages`. The warning at `:859` is emitted only *after* that crawl and does not stop the descent. Note the diff already contains the guard *pattern* for the sibling case (fetch failure, `:702-709`); the undated case has no equivalent.

Smallest fix (`src/gamarr/pipeline.py`): treat "a full call yielded pages and still no `max_month_seen`" like the outage case — break the year loop (or stop after the first such year) and keep the existing warning, so the diagnostic fires before the cost is paid.

`pipeline.py:219`; test at `tests/unit/test_pipeline.py:9956-9970`.

def test_a_mid_cycle_outage_stops_after_two_failed_years(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        """Once dates are seen, two dead years still mean a blind descent."""
        import datetime

        current_year = datetime.datetime.now(tz=datetime.UTC).year
        calls, logs = self._run(
            tmp_path=tmp_path,
            max_pages=3,
            max_date=201501,
            max_cycle_months=6,
            fail_years={current_year - 1, current_year - 2, current_year - 3},
        )
        years = [call["year"] for call in calls]
        assert years == [current_year, current_year - 1, current_year - 2], (
            f"a mid-cycle outage must stop the descent: {years}"
        )
        assert any("consecutive years failed to browse" in line for line in logs), logs

    def test_a_pace_wider_than_the_floor_shortens_without_crossing_it(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        """The pace may shorten the window but never opens years below the floor."""
        calls, _logs = self._run(
            tmp_path=tmp_path,
            max_pages=3,
            max_date=202001,
            max_cycle_months=24,
            games_for_year=lambda year: [{"title": "G", "slug": "g", "release_date": f"{year}-12-01"}],
        )
        years = [call["year"] for call in calls]
        assert years, "expected at least one probe"
        assert min(years) >= 2020, f"the floor year is the bottom of the window: {years}"
        assert len(years) < 5, f"the 24-month pace must shorten the window: {years}"

## Review

### Verified correct (round‑6 fixes re‑checked, not re‑reported)

1. **Outage stop no longer needs a date, and genuinely-empty years do not count as failures.** `pipeline.py:812-816` increments `failed_years_in_a_row` only when `mc._recent_games_failed is True` (set by `metacritic._classify_page` only for a `None` page — non‑200 or unparsable parse), and resets it on every non-failed call. A 200-with-no-games page sets `_recent_games_exhausted` instead (`metacritic.py:628-636`), so two consecutive healthy-but-empty years keep the streak at 0 and the descent continues. A `None` page for two consecutive years is a real outage signal, so the guard cannot fire on a healthy site. `pipeline.py:881` (exception path) also advances the streak as claimed.
2. **Unpaced warning covers the floor-span case.** `pipeline.py:608-613`: `floor_span > 0 and cfg.max_cycle_months >= floor_span` fires for a pace that can never bind. I checked it cannot false-positive: `floor_span` is measured from *today*, and the real anchor (`max_month_seen`) is always ≤ today, so `pace >= floor_span` implies `pace >= months(anchor, floor)` — the pace can never bind. The clause is one-directional (false negatives possible, no false positives).
3. **Summary/backlog-warning assertions exist** (`test_an_unpaced_date_window_is_reported_as_uncapped`, `test_a_backlog_date_cycle_reports_undated_pages_too`), **the pace-vs-floor test now returns year-shaped dates** (`test_a_pace_wider_than_the_floor_shortens_without_crossing_it`, which really does exercise the `_month_span` break), and **the floorless test is renamed to the slack bound** (`test_a_floorless_pace_stops_at_the_slack_bound`).
4. **Backlog is bit-identical.** `_date_driven(scan_order, False, max_date, _)` reduces to `bool(max_date) and scan_order == "new"`, the per-call branch body for backlog date mode is unchanged, `floor_cutoff` is the same value, and the only new guard (`pace_month > 0 and is_valid_year_month(...)`, `pipeline.py:750`) can only trigger for backlog when `pace_month < 195801`, where the old `max(pace_cutoff, floor_cutoff)` also picked the floor. Verified `reset_progress` (`pipeline.py:686, 927, 937`), `set_last_scanned_page` (`:803`), `sum_scanned_pages` and `set_cursor_sort_order` are all unreachable in latest mode, so "latest never reads/writes cursors" still holds on the date path.
5. **Single predicate.** `run_acquisition:400` normalises first and passes `"new" if mode == "latest" else sort_order`; `_run_discovery_phases:512` uses the coerced `scan_order`. The two cannot disagree, and `max_pages` is only clamped when `date_driven` is false (`:272-276`).

- **Finding: MEDIUM — the new behaviour on the exception path is untested.** `src/gamarr/pipeline.py:879-881` (`failed_years_in_a_row += 1` inside `except Exception`). Round‑6 fix #1 claims "the exception path now advances the streak", but every new test drives failures through the `_recent_games_failed` flag (`tests/unit/test_pipeline.py:9789-9816`); a grep of the test suite finds no case where `scan_recent_games` raises (`"Scan failed for year"`, `side_effect=…Error`: no matches). Concrete risk: if that increment is dropped in a later refactor, two consecutive years that raise (a client bug or a `TypeError` in the per-call setup) burn a full request/timeout each and the descent never stops — exactly the failure the fix was for. Smallest fix: add one test in `TestLatestMode` that sets `mock_mc.scan_recent_games.side_effect` to raise for the first two years and asserts `len(calls) == 2`, the `"consecutive years failed to browse"` warning, and no `"no listing was found"` warning (`fetch_failed` must suppress it). ## Review

**Scope:** the 7-file working-tree diff (`README.md`, plan, design spec, `config.py`, `pipeline.py`, `utils.py`, `tests/unit/test_pipeline.py`) against the intent: in `latest`, date keys drive the scan and `max_pages` is a fallback; latest never touches cursors; backlog unchanged. Round-7 fixes 1–6 re-verified.

### Correct

- **Intent matches the code.** `_date_driven` (`pipeline.py:223-245`) is the single predicate: `new`-order only, `max_date` wins, `max_cycle_months` only makes *latest* date-driven. `run_acquisition` computes it with the same order the pipeline resolves (`"new" if mode == "latest" else sort_order`, `pipeline.py:402`) and `_run_discovery_phases` recomputes it *after* the score-sort coercion (`pipeline.py:510`), so the normaliser and the scan cannot disagree — the only two reachable cases (backlog: `bool(max_date)`; latest: always `new`) are identical on both calls.
- **`max_pages` really is a fallback only.** In date mode `per_call_max = 0` (`pipeline.py:742`), the top-of-loop depth break is `latest_mode and not date_mode` (`pipeline.py:709`), and the depth reserve/decrement are in the `elif latest_mode` / `not date_mode` arms only. `test_max_cycle_months_wires_the_pace_and_max_pages_is_unused` and `test_max_date_and_pace_beat_max_pages` assert `max_pages == 0` on *every* call, not just the first.
- **No latest-mode cursor write or read is reachable.** `get_last_scanned_page` is only in the `else` of `start_page = 1 if latest_mode else …` (`pipeline.py:734`); `set_last_scanned_page` is gated by `not latest_mode` (`pipeline.py:805`); `reset_progress` sites are all inside `not latest_mode`/backlog arms (`pipeline.py:560, 681, 934, 944`); `set_cursor_sort_order` is backlog-only (`pipeline.py:561`). `test_a_date_driven_cycle_does_not_persist_cursors` seeds page 7 for 2025, which the cycle *does* visit, so an unguarded write or a `reset_progress` would fail it — the test has teeth.
- **Backlog is behaviourally identical.** `floor_cutoff = year_month_to_date(floor_month) if floor_month else None` and `if floor_month:` are equivalent to the old `if date_mode:` because `floor_month = cfg.max_date if date_mode else 0`; the `_date_driven("new", False, …)` result equals the old `bool(max_date) and scan_order == "new"`; the merge of the depth and date branches at the top of the loop is order-preserving for backlog (`pages_this_cycle >= max_pages_cfg` arm skipped in date mode, exactly as before). The only backlog-visible changes are new INFO/WARNING lines.
- **The pace/floor guard does not change backlog behaviour** (`pipeline.py:751-758`). For backlog `floor_cutoff` is always set, and any `pace_month < 195801` formats to a `"YYYY-MM-01"` string that sorts *below* any valid floor, so the old unconditional `max(pace_cutoff, floor_cutoff)` yielded the floor — the same value the guard now keeps.
- **The descent is bounded and reaches every reachable anchor.** Floored: `cutoff_year = floor_month // 100`, so the floor year is always iterated and no year below it (`test_a_floor_alone_bounds_latest_without_pacing`, `test_the_year_bound_is_the_floor_not_a_derived_bound`). Floorless: `max(1958, anchor - (2·⌈months/12⌉ + 3))`, and the year loop cannot go below 1958 (`test_a_huge_pace_bounds_at_the_catalogue_floor`). If the real anchor lies *below* the bound, every probed year is empty → `pages_this_cycle == 0` → the "no listing was found from X down to Y — the paced window may lie below it" warning fires (`pipeline.py:890-908`), so truncation is always reported, never silent. The doubled slack costs at most one request per empty year (page 1 of an empty listing does not trigger the drain re-probe, `_needs_drain_confirmation` requires `page_number > 1`), so it does probe years it does not need, but cheaply and visibly.
- **Fail streak on both failure paths.** `failed_years_in_a_row` is incremented in the `except` (`pipeline.py:912`) and in the `_recent_games_failed` branch (`pipeline.py:818`), reset on any success, and checked at the top of the *next* iteration, so two raising years give exactly two calls (`test_two_raising_years_stop_the_descent`), and one failed year still lets the next one run (`test_a_fetch_outage_stops_the_descent_before_the_anchor`). The streak guard is `latest_mode`-and-`date_mode`-gated, so backlog keeps crawling a broken year (as required).
- **Fail streak vs undated guard cannot interact badly.** The two are independent: the streak resets to 0 on the undated-but-successful call, so no spurious "consecutive failures" break; the undated flag can only be set before any dated game exists in the cycle (`max_month_seen is None`), i.e. when there is no anchor to pace at all; a call cannot be both failed and exhausted (`_classify_page` returns on the failure path before the empty-page branch, `metacritic.py:556-580`).

- Undated-listing guard now runs *after* this call's `min_month_seen`/`max_month_seen` update (`pipeline.py:845-862`), so a drained-but-dated year no longer trips it; `test_a_drained_year_with_dates_keeps_the_descent` (`test_pipeline.py:10023`) and `test_undated_pages_are_reported_and_stop_the_descent` (`10063`) both pin the two directions.

Reachability holds for the intended case (lag ≤ pace+3 years leaves the bound at or below the window bottom) and the range is finite for every pace ≤ 1200.
- The "effectively unpaced" test no longer consults the floorless bound when a floor is set (`pipeline.py:616-619`: `not floor_month and …`), confirmed by `test_a_floor_limited_whole_window_is_reported_too` and `test_max_date_and_pace_beat_max_pages` (no warning at pace 12 / floor 202401).

`src/gamarr/pipeline.py:612-634` (condition `floor_span > 0 and cfg.max_cycle_months >= floor_span`, message at `628-633`), with the same advice in `README.md:192` ("set `max_cycle_months` to pace it").

The window is 10 months; re-reading it each cycle is exactly the documented latest contract (`README.md:345`: "it restarts from the newest page every cycle"). With `max_date` auto-clamped to the current month, `floor_span == 0` suppresses the warning entirely — the same config space, opposite outcome.

Months 2024-01…2026-04 are therefore never read by any cycle, while the operator believed they had set "the oldest month you want reviewed" — the framing `README.md:194` and `README.md:479-480` use for `max_date`.
- The advice is wrong in latest mode: there are no cursors, so a *smaller* pace does not spread the sweep over cycles, it permanently narrows the reviewed window; the existing warning text and the README "set `max_cycle_months` to pace it" both read as if later cycles continue where the last stopped.

Files: `src/gamarr/pipeline.py`, `README.md`.

`tests/unit/test_pipeline.py:9900-9909` (`test_max_cycle_months_wires_the_pace_and_max_pages_is_unused`); the guard under test is `pipeline.py:719-721` (`latest_mode and not date_mode`).

A date-driven cycle with `max_pages: 3` then stops after 3 pages instead of the 6 the pace window allows (`max_cycle_months: 2`, no floor → bound `current−5`), i.e. exactly the regression this change exists to prevent. Every test still passes:
  - `test_max_cycle_months_wires_the_pace_and_max_pages_is_unused` asserts only `calls[0]` fields and log lines — the helper makes one page per call, and no assertion counts calls.
  - `test_a_floor_alone_bounds_latest_without_pacing` and `test_max_date_and_pace_beat_max_pages` use `max_pages=3` with a floor exactly 3 years back, so a 3-page cap yields the same year list; `len(calls) > 1` does not discriminate.

def test_a_drained_year_with_dates_keeps_the_descent(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        """A drained but dated listing is not evidence of an undated site."""
        import datetime

        current_year = datetime.datetime.now(tz=datetime.UTC).year
        floor_month = (current_year - 2) * 100 + 1
        calls, logs = self._run(tmp_path=tmp_path, max_pages=3, max_date=floor_month, exhausted=True)
        years = [call["year"] for call in calls]
        assert years == [current_year, current_year - 1, current_year - 2], (
            f"the descent must continue to the floor year: {years}"
        )
        assert not any("a whole listing carried no release dates" in line for line in logs), logs

    def test_the_client_cutoff_stop_ends_the_descent(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        """A client-reported cutoff must end the latest descent, not be ignored."""
        import datetime

        current_year = datetime.datetime.now(tz=datetime.UTC).year
        calls, _logs = self._run(
            tmp_path=tmp_path, max_pages=3, max_date=200001, cutoff_years={current_year}
        )
        years = [call["year"] for call in calls]
        assert years == [current_year], f"the cutoff stop must end the descent: {years}"

**No HIGH or MEDIUM findings.** Every finding below is LOW (comment/doc wording, log-message precision, test hygiene).

### Correct (with evidence)

- **Date-driven latest cannot be page-capped.** All four cap sites are closed for `latest + date_mode`: the loop head takes `elif date_mode:` (`pipeline.py:717-737`) so `pages_this_cycle >= max_pages_cfg` is unreachable; `per_call_max = 0` (`pipeline.py:742-757`); `remaining_pages -= pages_scanned` is `not date_mode`-guarded (`pipeline.py:891`); `cycle_allowance`/`remaining_pages` are zeroed in the `if latest_mode:` branch (`pipeline.py:668-670`). `_latest_call_depth` is now only on the depth path.
- **Latest never reads or writes cursors on the new path.** `start_page = 1 if latest_mode` (`:740`), `set_last_scanned_page` is `not latest_mode`-guarded (`:811`), both `reset_progress` calls are inside `date_mode and not latest_mode` / `not latest_mode` (`:926`, `:942`), `set_cursor_sort_order` only in the backlog branch (`:563`). Pinned by `test_a_date_driven_cycle_does_not_persist_cursors`.
- **No date-driven stall or unbounded *iteration*.** The year loop is a bounded `range(current_year, cutoff_year-1, -1)`; the floorless bound is `max(1958, year-(2p+3))` and the floored bound is absolute (`floor_month // 100`), never derived from today — so a stale anchor is not silently truncated (pinned by `test_the_year_bound_is_the_floor_not_a_derived_bound`).
- **Backlog semantics are unchanged**: `floor_cutoff` is equivalent to the old `if date_mode` guard (floor is non-zero whenever backlog is date-driven, `:514-516`); `if floor_month:` vs `if date_mode:` for `_games_at_or_after_floor` differs only in the new floorless case where it is a no-op; the new `pace_month >= 1958*100+1` guard (`:755-762`) resolves to the floor anyway when a floor exists, and it is what prevents `max(None, ...)` from crashing on the floorless path.
- **The "effectively unpaced" warning no longer fires for a paced floored window**: it requires `not cfg.max_cycle_months` **or** `floorless_catalogue_wide` (`:616-624`), and `floorless_catalogue_wide` is only true when the synthetic bound clamps to `EARLIEST_BROWSE_YEAR`. The three shapes are covered by `test_a_huge_pace_bounds_at_the_catalogue_floor`, `test_a_floor_covering_pace_is_not_called_unpaced`, `test_a_narrow_pace_states_its_scope`.
- **The new mocks are truthful, not just convenient.** `_recent_games_exhausted` with one collected page is reachable in production (page 1 collected, page 2 empty → `_finish_scan` reports `last_page = 1`, `pages_scanned = 1`); a failed fetch really does leave `last_page = 0` from `max(page_number-1, 0)`; `_recent_games_cutoff_reached` with games collected is reachable (collect pages 1..k, trip on k+1). `cutoff_years`'s arbitrary `"2024-01-01"` is correctly *not* the floor, so `floor_stop` is false and the break is exercised.
- **Only one calendar coupling found in the new tests**, and it does not go red (see F6). All other clock-derived years are used relative to `now()`, so they cannot flip.

### Findings (all LOW)

**F1 — LOW — docs: README promises "re-checked immediately in latest mode", which the new narrow-pace path makes false.**
`README.md:32-34` and `README.md:63-64` say failed/unpublished games "are re-checked when a browse pass next reaches their pages (immediately in `latest` mode …)". `pipeline.py:625-631` (added here) now states the opposite for a paced latest: "Latest mode reads the newest N month(s) only — … the older months are covered in backlog mode". Failure scenario: `mode: latest`, `max_date: 202001`, `max_cycle_months: 2` — a game released 3 months ago that had no scores yet is never re-checked in latest, contradicting the feature bullet the user read.
